audit_groups.finding: For open normal H, finite normal cores of kernels of finite prime-group quotients give exactly the original ambient intersection. Openness and normality are explicit; no argument for a nonopen subgroup is silently used.

The linear image of H is a prime-group because rho kills its maximal pro-prime residual. First-order coefficients and affine translations extend it by prime-groups. Vanishing at the original kernel generators and the original closed-normal-kernel condition force descent. Both the representation and cyclotomic twist are pulled back.

The original open-subgroup finiteness condition makes all base finite-module cocycles finite in number. Their finite affine kernels and the representation/character kernels yield one ambient open normal subgroup containing the residual subgroup. Original tower convergence then matches all base evaluations at fixed truncation.

With v=-y(c)/2, delta(v)(c)=y(c). Local witnesses become Y_j-v. Normalizing a global boundary gives the c-fixed primitive (w+beta(c)w)/2. The quotient injection is well defined and injective, with no extra factor of two.

Eventual representation equality and trivial cyclotomic twist at detecting elements make the eta-trace of the local boundary times R(sigma) zero by cyclicity of trace. The restricted quotient embeds in the already bounded polarized detecting quotient.

The restricted upstairs cocycle set is finite because its quotient and boundary subgroup are finite. A separate finite cardinality assertion for all tower cocycles is unnecessary. The level threshold may depend on m; the same detecting constant does not.
